GAP [1]: The mechanism by which sorafenib's inhibition of cyclin-dependent kinases leads to cell cycle arrest and apoptosis is unknown.
GAP [2]: No study has tested whether the depletion of cysteine interacts with sorafenib's ferroptosis-inducing effects in HCC cells.
GAP [3]: It is unclear whether sorafenib's disruption of SCD1-mediated fatty acid synthesis acts upstream or downstream of the ATP-AMPK-mTOR-SREBP1 signaling pathway.
GAP [4]: The causal path by which low-dose sorafenib treatment prevents NASH progression involves unknown mechanisms and pathways.
GAP [5]: It is unclear whether the dosing regimen of 200 mg twice daily for FLT3-ITD and ERK inhibition has a significant impact on downstream signaling pathways.
